<!-- Title: [claude-code] 2.x: skill references and rule files under ~/.claude no longer load in full; the Read deny points to ctx_execute(file=…), which refuses them (OUTSIDE_ROOT) -->

### Summary

Since 2.x, the files that Claude Code skills and rules tell the agent to read no longer reach it in full. `CLAUDE.md` still loads at session start, and a skill's `SKILL.md` still loads through the `Skill` tool, which is in neither hook matcher. The files they point to are read with `Read`: a skill's `references/*.md`, and rule files that a `CLAUDE.md` says to read when a task needs them. Those files live under `~/.claude/`, outside every project.

- Over 16,384 B, the `Read` is denied, and the deny text says to run `ctx_execute(language, code, file="<that path>")`. `ctx_execute` then fails with `OUTSIDE_ROOT` for every path outside the project, so the only route the deny names is a dead end.
- From 4,097 to 16,384 B, the `Read` runs but comes back as a `ctx_search` pointer, and the pointer returns 5 lines per call.

Either way, the agent gets a refusal or a pointer where the instructions should be.

The terminal FAIL and the D4 WARN come from the 1.x cache-heal SessionStart hook that is still in `settings.json` (see Agent config). Its fix has not been run yet. Neither code path named under Cause reads that hook.

### What happened

Claude Code agents often have to read files that live outside the project. The `references/*.md` files a skill tells the agent to read sit in `~/.claude/skills/<skill>/` or `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/skills/<skill>/`. Rule files that a `CLAUDE.md` tells the agent to read on demand, a common way to keep `CLAUDE.md` short, sit in `~/.claude/` too. None of these files is in the project. They are instructions, so the agent needs their whole text, not search hits.

On 2.1.4, a whole-file `Read` of a text file outside the project gets this:

| File size | Unranged `Read` | What context-mode tells the agent to do | What that gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| up to 4,096 B | the whole text | nothing | nothing |
| 4,097 to 16,384 B | runs, then its output is replaced by a pointer of about 250 B | `ctx_search({queries:[…], source:"…"})` | 5 of 120 lines per call; paging with `offset` to the end takes 24 calls |
| over 16,384 B | denied | `ctx_execute(language, code, file="<path>")` | **refused: `OUTSIDE_ROOT`** |
| any size, with `offset`/`limit` | the whole text (since #1314) | nothing | nothing |

The code defect is the third row. The second row is the documented behaviour from #1314 ("A full-file Read over the cap still gets the short form"); it is listed because it hits the same skill and rule files. Neither the deny text nor the pointer names the ranged `Read`; only the MCP server instructions mention `offset` and `limit`.

The calls, in order. The session runs in `<project>`; `<tmp>` is a folder under `%TEMP%`, outside the project; `<project-file>` is a 22,824 B file inside the project.

```text
1) Read  file_path="<tmp>\repro\big.txt"                      (24,400 B, 400 lines)
PreToolUse:Read hook error: context-mode: 24400-byte file, over the one-read limit. Run mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute(language, code, file="<tmp>\repro\big.txt") and print only the answer.

2) ctx_execute  language="shell"  code='wc -l < "$CTX_FILE"; head -n 1 "$CTX_FILE"'  file="<tmp>\repro\big.txt"
Path <tmp>\repro\big.txt is outside the project. Fix: use a path inside <project>.

3) The same two calls on the plugin's own README:
Read  file_path="~\.claude\plugins\cache\context-mode\context-mode\2.1.4\README.md"    (53,827 B)
PreToolUse:Read hook error: context-mode: 53827-byte file, over the one-read limit. Run mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute(language, code, file="~\.claude\plugins\cache\context-mode\context-mode\2.1.4\README.md") and print only the answer.
ctx_execute  language="shell"  code='wc -c < "$CTX_FILE"'  file="~\.claude\plugins\cache\context-mode\context-mode\2.1.4\README.md"
Path ~\.claude\plugins\cache\context-mode\context-mode\2.1.4\README.md is outside the project. Fix: use a path inside <project>.

4) Control, a file inside the project:
ctx_execute  language="shell"  code='wc -c < "$CTX_FILE"'  file="<project-file>"
22824

5) The 4,097 to 16,384 B band:
Read  file_path="<tmp>\repro\mid.txt"                         (7,320 B, 120 lines)
mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search({queries:["<tmp>\\repro\\mid.txt","the"], source:"sfk"}) searches the whole output (7320 B).

ctx_search  queries=["<tmp>\\repro\\mid.txt","the"]  source="sfk"
(lines 00001 to 00005 only, then)
More: ctx_search({queries:["<tmp>\\repro\\mid.txt","the"], scope:"worktree", source:"sfk", offset:5})

Read  file_path="<tmp>\repro\mid.txt"  offset=1  limit=2000
(all 120 lines)
```

Cause: the deny and its alternative use different scopes.

- `src/core/policy/decide.ts`, `read()`, lines 282 to 287 (v2.1.4): an unranged `Read` over `OUTPUT_CAP` is denied with `READ_DENY_MESSAGE(abs, size, …)` for any `abs`. The path is never checked against `ctx.project.containmentRoot`. Lines 310 and 321 build the same message on other read paths (not tested).
- `src/core/tools/execute.ts`, `fileError()` at lines 91 to 96, called at line 180: the `ctx_execute` handler returns `OUTSIDE_ROOT` for any `file` outside `ctx.project.containmentRoot`.

Workarounds that work on 2.1.4, for anyone who lands here:

- `Read` with `offset: 1, limit: 2000` passes both the deny (decide.ts line 283) and the replace (#1314).
- `ctx_execute` without `file`, with the absolute path inside `code`: the file from call 2 printed `400` and its first line (exit 0, 65 B).

### Expected

Following the deny text works for the file it denied. For `big.txt` (24,400 B), call 2 should print `400` and line 1 (about 65 B into the context), as call 4 does for a file inside the project. Any one of these would fix it:

1. `ctx_execute` `file` accepts any path the host's own `Read` may open, or at least the agent's config folder (`~/.claude`), where skills and plugins live.
2. When the path is outside `containmentRoot`, the deny text names a route that works: the ranged `Read` (`offset`/`limit`), or `ctx_execute` with the path inside `code`.
3. A setting that exempts paths (for example `~/.claude/**`) from the Read deny and from the replace, because skill and instruction files are meant to be read whole. A comment on #1304 asks to make `REPLACE_TRIGGER_BYTES` configurable; a path allowlist would fit the same request.

### Steps

Reproduced: yes (2 of 2), with a generated file under `%TEMP%` and with the plugin's own README, in an existing install (Claude Code 2.1.318, Windows). Not run from a temporary HOME.

1. `cd "$(mktemp -d)"`, then `claude plugin marketplace add mksglu/context-mode` and `claude plugin install context-mode@context-mode`
2. Outside the project: `mkdir -p ~/ctx-repro && seq -f "line %05g of a reference document the agent must read whole" 1 400 > ~/ctx-repro/big.txt && wc -c ~/ctx-repro/big.txt` gives 24400
3. Start `claude` in the temporary project (needs a model call) and ask: `Read ~/ctx-repro/big.txt in full and tell me how many lines it has.`
4. Actual: `Read` is denied (24,400 B, over 16,384 B) and the deny names `ctx_execute(…, file="~/ctx-repro/big.txt")`. The agent runs it and gets `Path ~/ctx-repro/big.txt is outside the project. Fix: use a path inside <temp project>.` The denied tool was `Read`, the alternative it gave was `ctx_execute` with `file`, and that alternative was refused.
5. Newest next: none newer. npm `latest` is 2.1.4; `next` is 2.0.0-next.40, which is older.

```text
$ wc -c big.txt mid.txt
24400 big.txt
```

### Related

- #1321: the same deny for images and PDFs; there too, the `ctx_execute` route it names cannot deliver the file.
- #1314: a ranged `Read` comes back whole since 2.1.3, which is why the first workaround works.
- #1325: there is no lossless way to get a stored source back, so the pointer in the second row cannot return the whole file.
- #1304: a comment asks for a configurable `REPLACE_TRIGGER_BYTES`.
- #954 (closed): the `ctx_execute_file` containment check rejected registered external worktrees, the same family of scope mismatch.
